messages:
Security Ops: @here Advisory: new enforced policy — service credentials with TTLs >24h will be automatically revoked after a 14-day grace period. This reduces blast radius for leaks. Read required actions below. :rotating_light:

Maria Chen: Quick Q — does this hit credentials managed in Vault that rotate automatically?

Security Ops: If Vault rotates them and the effective TTL is under 24h, you're fine. Enforcement targets static keys and tokens listed in the inventory as >24h.

Aj Patel: Some CI jobs still use static deploy keys. Any recommended migration pattern?

Security Ops: Use OIDC or short-lived token flows. Example for GH Actions:
```
- name: Configure AWS credentials
  uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v2
  with:
    role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/github-actions
```
If you can't migrate immediately, open an exception ticket (tag: ephemeral-exception) and include compensating controls.

Lina Gomez: How do I find services affected?

Security Ops: Owners with inventory access can run the query in the inventory dashboard. We'll also publish a CSV at https://internal.redwood/policies/pc-2026-04.

SRE oncall: Timeline: dry-run audit next Tuesday (no revokes), enforcement after 14 days. We'll post exact times.

Aj Patel: Copy. We'll migrate CI and update here when done.

Security Ops: Action items: audit tokens, migrate to <24h or OIDC, rotate static keys now, open exception ticket if needed. We're scheduling a brief Q&A and checklist doc.

deploy-bot: policy-change created: service-credentials-ttl-enforcement (id: pc-2026-04).

Maria Chen: Starting rotation now.

Lina Gomez: Opening exception ticket for legacy batch jobs.

SRE oncall: We'll review exceptions within 48h. Ping me for pairing.
